mainEntity.name: What is the median home price in Madison, WI right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: The median sale price in Madison was $440,000 in August 2026, up 8.6% from the prior year. Year-to-date through September 2026, the median also sits at $440,000 — up 3.5% from 2025's full-year figure of $424,900.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to sell a house in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: The median days on market was 8 days in August 2026 — unchanged year-over-year. Half of all homes sold went under contract within eight days of listing. The average of 20 days reflects a smaller group of slower-moving listings pulling the average up.

mainEntity.name: Is Madison, WI a buyer's or seller's market right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Madison is an Extreme Seller's Market. With 1.96 months of supply — well below the 2-month threshold for that tier — sellers hold significant leverage. Buyers are still paying an average of 0.43% over asking price across the city, with several upper price brackets running well over 2% over list.

mainEntity.name: How many homes sold in Madison in August 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: 203 homes sold in August 2026, down 13.6% from 235 sales in August 2025. Total volume was $100,374,371 — down 6.5% year-over-year, reflecting fewer transactions rather than falling prices.

mainEntity.name: What is the cheapest area to buy a home in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: In August 2026, zip 53704 had the lowest median sale among higher-volume zips at $394,900 (29 sales) — also the most active zip in the city by transaction count. Zip 53714 traded slightly lower at $395,000 on a smaller sample of 13 sales.

mainEntity.name: Which Madison zip code has the most expensive homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zip 53705 posted the highest median among higher-volume zips at $685,000 in August 2026, off 14 sales. Zip 53717 followed at $515,000 (16 sales) and 53711 at $513,250 (19 sales).

mainEntity.name: Are home prices going up or down in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: Up. Prices rose 8.6% year-over-year to $440,000 in August 2026. Madison has posted consistent gains since 2018, when the median was $260,000 — a 69% increase over eight years.

mainEntity.name: Should I wait for interest rates to drop before buying in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: The risk of waiting in Madison is real. Prices have increased every year since 2018. If rates drop and you refinance later, you're still ahead. If prices rise another 5–8% while you wait — roughly Madison's recent annual pace — the savings may not offset the higher purchase price. Buy when the payment makes sense, and refinance when rates improve.

mainEntity.name: How many homes are currently for sale in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of September 1, 2026, there are 436 active listings in Madison and 101 homes pending. The median time from list to pending is 8 days.

mainEntity.name: What price range is most competitive in Madison right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: The $300,000–$399,999 range is the tightest, with just 1.61 months of supply and 82 active listings against 51 average sales per month. The $400,000–$499,999 range is close behind at 1.68 months and is the most active bracket overall, with 104 active listings and 62 average sales per month.

mainEntity.name: Can buyers negotiate on price in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most price ranges, not easily. The city-wide average was 0.43% over asking in August. Buyers at the entry level have a bit more room — the $100,000–$199,999 bracket has recently traded around 1.0% under asking. In other ranges, focus your negotiation on terms rather than price.

mainEntity.name: Is now a good time to sell a home in Madison?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Median DOM of 8 days, 1.96 months of supply, and buyers still paying over asking in most brackets — these are solid seller conditions. Price competitively, present well, and Madison's market will do the rest.
